question: I recently read in a security blog: "The APT maintains a persistent presence on compromised machines by using a Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) rootkit called Lojax. This rootkit lives within the computer’s flash memory, allowing Fancy Bear to maintain persistence even if the hard drive of a compromised machine is replaced or the operating system is reinstalled." Please provide: 1) the MITRE ATT&CK category (including its ID) that maps to this behavior; 2) an explanation of how this behavior maps to the technique; and 3) which operating systems are affected according to the technique (e.g., Linux, macOS, Windows, ESXi)?
answer: 1) T1542.001 - System Firmware. 2) Mapping Explanation: The behavior of installing a UEFI rootkit (Lojax) into flash memory for persistence directly aligns with the System Firmware category, as it involves compromising the system firmware to survive reinstallation or hardware replacement. 3) Applicable Platforms: Windows and Network Devices.
